newsitem.title: USA: NYSE chief sees 16-20 hour trading days.
newsitem.headline: NYSE chief sees 16-20 hour trading days.

text.p: New York Stock Exchange Chairman Richard Grasso said on Thursday that eventually the exchange will have trading for 16 to 20 hours a day.
He said in a speech to the Houston Forum Club that the hours would be expanded to accomodate an expected increase in foreign companies listed on the exchange.
"As we begin to assemble critical mass in the product base, we will tap the constituencies both here in the U.S. and outside as to their desire to see our hours stretched," he said.
"We will over the course of the next decade end up being a 16-to-20 hour a day market, multi-currency in both quotation and settlement and cross-currency for U.S. securities," Grasso said.
He said there are currently 300 foreign stocks on the exchange, but that the number was expected to double by the end of this decade and double again in the following 10 years.
There are currently a total of about 3,000 stocks listed, he said.
Grasso also said in a discussion about program trading that the exchange was satisfied with current "circuit-breakers" in place to slow big swings in the market.
"The circuit traders and shock absorbers that have been introduced to try to slow the process indeed do work," he said. "We have no inclination whatsoever to change those safety valves."
